configuration.enablement: Disabled by default. Select `TERM001`, or the `TERM` prefix, and configure `terms` under `[tool.stilyagi.rule.TERM001]`. The builtin plugin gate still applies: `plugins = []` disables all builtin rules, and `lint.ignore`, per-file ignores, and suppression directives still apply. Without a nonempty `terms` list the rule is inactive even when selected.

constraints: Must be an array of strings.
Each entry must be exactly one alphabetic word under `str.isalpha`; spaces, punctuation, numerals, and empty strings are rejected.
Duplicates coalesce after the configured comparison.
options.description: Words to report when they appear as whole prose tokens.
options.name: terms

options.description: Compare configured terms against tokens using exact case instead of Unicode case folding.
options.name: case_sensitive

variants.description: Use Unicode `casefold()` for the configured term and the candidate token. This is the default.
Compare the configured spelling exactly. Neither mode promises Unicode normalization or locale-aware matching.

rule.explanation: Every configured term is matched against whole alphabetic tokens, so `obviously` never matches inside `unobviously`. The `TOKENS` capability is supplied by the builtin pack's in-process tokenizer; no NLP model or external provider is loaded. When `case_sensitive` is false, which is the default, both the configured term and the token are compared with Unicode `casefold()`; when it is true, the exact spelling is compared. Duplicate terms coalesce under the chosen comparison. The rule is opt-in and does nothing until terms are configured.
rule.fixes: The rule offers no fix. Choosing a replacement for a banned term is editorial, so no edit is planned and `--fix` leaves the source unchanged.
limitations: Only headings, paragraphs, and table cells are inspected; code blocks, inline code, link destinations, and frontmatter are not.

Matching is whole-token only, but hyphens, punctuation, and digits are token boundaries: a term can match one word inside a hyphenated or punctuated form. Use an exact context check when that is too broad.
The opposite editorial policy, requiring a term rather than banning it, is not supported; no inverse rule or option exists in this slice.
Neither case mode promises locale-aware matching or Unicode normalization; use `case_sensitive = true` when exact spelling matters.
Configuration, per-file ignores, and suppression directives can stop a finding; static metadata does not describe effective enablement for a particular file.
rule.name: banned-term
rule.summary: Report configured banned terms in prose.
